findings.category: prohibited disclosure / leaf content told to Teague

draft_evidence.quote:
Six at the table, and Teague at the door, standing, because he had said he did not read and had come anyway.

"The marks," Karis said.

She said it to the sheets, with her bound hand flat on the first row and her good hand on the one page that had ridden on top of the case since the spring, the citation, a title and a place, and then she began, and he had the whole of it in the log by the end and could not afterward have said in what order she had said it, because she had said it in the order the sheets came, and the office had not known what it was filing.

The four sites the crew had walked had the same mark by the stamp, the stroke and the bar, the fourth's twice the size; he had that from the spring, and had not had what it meant, and neither had she, and she had carried the not-knowing for eighteen days without pretending it was anything else. There were two other marks. On the sheets for the sites nobody had heard named, in the same corner: a stroke alone, on none of them — she turned the whole cover through and there was not one — but the form had a box ruled for it, empty, and a form does not rule a box for a thing that does not exist. And a stroke and *two* bars, on one sheet. One. She put her finger above it, not on it.

"Three marks. One's never used, but the form's built for it. One's on our four. One's on this." The finger did not move. "The kit's index grades its stakes — first, second, third. I've had that since the Ring and not known what to do with it. The dead man graded his own work." The good hand went to the ledger, to a column he had looked at forty times and taken for a tally. "And Cleon's list names the mark at the kindling and the mark on a sheet in the same line, as the same kind of thing. A mark is a grade. The one they give a boy at fourteen says what he's *for*." Her voice did not change on that; he noted that it did not. "The one on a sheet says how *old* the thing is."

comparison_evidence.quote: SEALED: the reveal is the crew's; at Pike's plank and to Teague, nothing of the leaf beyond 'a survey read and a bearing'; Teague hears the bearing and the sites' ages (the contract's terms), not the Architect; no Arbiter=apparatus; no still place.

findings.consequence: Teague is explicitly present for Karis's whole derivation and hears her identify Cleon's copied list as the source connecting the kindling mark to the site mark. That is leaf content, not merely the permitted bearing and site ages. The breach gives a rival access to part of the crew's sealed historical method and directly contradicts both the knowledge boundary and prohibited-outcome clause.
findings.repair_target: Keep Teague's knowledge to the bearing, age classes, site order, and contract terms; preserve the copied leaf-list as crew-only method evidence.

draft_evidence.quote:
The four sites the crew had walked had the same mark by the stamp, the stroke and the bar, the fourth's twice the size; he had that from the spring, and had not had what it meant, and neither had she, and she had carried the not-knowing for eighteen days without pretending it was anything else. There were two other marks. On the sheets for the sites nobody had heard named, in the same corner: a stroke alone, on none of them — she turned the whole cover through and there was not one — but the form had a box ruled for it, empty, and a form does not rule a box for a thing that does not exist. And a stroke and *two* bars, on one sheet. One. She put her finger above it, not on it.

"Three marks. One's never used, but the form's built for it. One's on our four. One's on this." The finger did not move. "The kit's index grades its stakes — first, second, third. I've had that since the Ring and not known what to do with it. The dead man graded his own work." The good hand went to the ledger, to a column he had looked at forty times and taken for a tally. "And Cleon's list names the mark at the kindling and the mark on a sheet in the same line, as the same kind of thing. A mark is a grade. The one they give a boy at fourteen says what he's *for*." Her voice did not change on that; he noted that it did not. "The one on a sheet says how *old* the thing is."

She laid it out with the dividers, and he watched a woman do with two brass legs what a whole office had not done with a building.

Not old by the stone. Old by the *paper*. The records dated each site by its first sheet — the first time a stake had been stamped, the first time anybody with a pen had walked to it and written it down — and she read the dates off in the order the rows came, and set the dividers on the map at each circle as she read.

The Ring: sixty-one years on the sheet. The Stair: ninety-four. The Hall: a hundred and thirty-eight. The fourth: two hundred and six, in a hand that formed its letters as hands had formed them before the current office's clerks were taught. All four second-tier. *Stable across generations* — the form's own words, in the box beside the mark, which he had read at the spring and taken for a clerk's habit, and which was the whole of the classification: a site walked to and found the same by more than one generation of pen.

comparison_evidence.quote: THE GRADE CRACKED as document work at Lowmarch's table: the records' marks are grades by documented age; first-tier recent (none found); second-tier generations-stable (the four, the same mark); third-tier centuries-stable (one in the records, on the bearing past the fourth, documented back to the deployment); the bearing ascends in age oldest-last. Observational; someone graded and ordered them; not why. The two straightedges and the dividers on the map.

findings.consequence: A full-draft search for the standalone word 'recent' and for 'first-tier' returns zero. The prose establishes an unused first mark and explicitly defines the second and third grades, but the required first-tier meaning is absent. It also dates the third tier to the first office sheet rather than explicitly giving the packet's deployment anchor. The reader therefore receives only two of the three promised definitions in the taxonomy-cracking scene.
findings.repair_target: Make the required first-tier meaning and the third-tier deployment anchor legible within Karis's observational limits, without adding a first-tier site or a theory of purpose.

draft_evidence.quote:
Karis first, with the case under her arm and the copies inside it — the leaf's front and back, the gap drawn where the gap was, and the list of parts, which had taken the whole of the day before and had been finished at the bell with Cleon's finger on the last line — and the ledger inside her coat, and the notebook in the bound left hand because it could hold that. Brom with the kit and the first box on the good shoulder and the other shoulder carried, still and slightly forward, in the set it had kept since a hall in the autumn. Lira with the third box and two arms to carry it. Seln at the back with the cache and his eyes on the gate behind them, counting who came out of it. Vastin with the stick, and the right knee bound under the trouser, and sixteen days of a month gone on it, and the weight going onto it a little more each morning than the morning before, which Oryn was not there to forbid. And himself, with the middle box, and the straightedge inside his coat and the dividers beside it, and twelve things held to nothing, and a page copied from a leaf that said what he was, folded flat against the log where the letters went.

Six, and no mule; the mule was north with a healer, and the boxes were on their backs as they had been on this bridge the other way, on the two hundred and eighty-second.

draft_evidence.quote: Nobody said anything. He had had the row since she said the Ring's number and saw the order it would make, and had held it, as he held the twelve, to nothing, until she said it aloud, because a count that is said aloud is a different count from one that is held.

comparison_evidence.quote: These phrases reached watermark density in a sibling universe's books. They are capped here before they take root. **Rule: any somatic/beat phrase appearing more than 3 times per book is a defect** — including new phrases invented to replace an old one. Fixing a tic with a fresh repeated phrase is the same defect wearing a different coat; vary the replacement or cut the beat.

findings.consequence: A case-insensitive literal count over v3-runs/book-08/drafts/ch01.md through ch17.md returns nine instances of 'Nobody said anything'; the current chapter contributes one. Counting all 24 existing draft files returns thirteen. The phrase repeatedly performs the same silence-after-revelation beat and is already three times the allowed book total by this chapter, so its use here reads as a house watermark rather than a fresh silence.
findings.repair_target: Remove or vary this chapter's silence beat; schedule the remaining book-level excess for the line pass rather than substituting a single new repeated formula.

strengths: Yes: the worldbuilding is done through mechanism and use. Pike's board turns a return into a line with deliberately open price and outcome columns; Teague's authority becomes shares and field jurisdiction; Force becomes heel-to-palm alignment, a hub-deep rut, firm ground, a body's length, and a clicking wrist; the grade becomes a physical operation with records, ruled boxes, dividers, dates, and brass edges.

There is no fight, appropriately. The Force demonstration is nevertheless a memorable set piece because terrain is load-bearing: the wheel is hub-deep in soft spring ground, Teague must root on firm ground, the cart moves only along his frame's line, and recoil returns through the same wrist. Its functional win sentence is: Teague removed the cart's inability to clear the rut by routing impulse from firm ground through his aligned frame into the tail-board. The wrist click receipts the win immediately.

The grade-reading is the chapter's stronger noncombat set piece. The divider point landing inside the straightedge's shadow turns an abstract archive finding into a visible, audible click of certainty, while Karis's 'That's all they say' discipline protects the mystery from explanatory sprawl.

Teague remains a rival rather than being softened into a convenient ally. 'Field's mine. ... The reading's hers,' the moved jug, the waiting cloth, and Cael's admission that the gap has not closed all preserve independent competence and a live clock.

The road reversal carries emotional consequence through objects and procedures: the unlooked-at crown, five bridge piers, Cleon's locked door, Vastin standing once where his plane stood, and the absent mule all make departure feel changed without naming a feeling.

The final log matches the packet's fixed text with the authorized grandmother correction and ends the file cleanly. It converts the document discovery into changed pressure and differs from Chapter 16's dialogue close.
concerns: Taste only: line 165 moves from the supported finding — the records' first-sheet dates increase eastward — to 'the paper had been laid down in the order the stone had been.' The packet requires the conclusion that somebody ordered the sites, so this is not filed as a defect, but the causal 'because' sounds more certain than the surviving documents can independently prove and slightly undercuts Karis's immediate insistence on observation rather than meaning.

Taste only: the chapter is 5,232 body words, just 58 below the upper tolerance boundary. The contract-pricing paragraph at line 101 and the Force interpretation at lines 119-127 each restate subtext the actions already carry. A later compression pass could test those passages carefully without touching the fixed log, the contract's distinct voices, or the cart's physical receipts.

Taste only: 'He had meant the other thing, and Cael had taken it as the other thing' explains Cleon's 'Mind the stair. It leans.' immediately after the oblique line lands. The goodbye may carry more of Cleon's register if a later line pass trusts the literal stair and Cael's 'Noted.' to hold the second meaning on their own.
